# Design, Innovation and Sports Awards
- **[16 Nov 2026] Red Dot: Best of the Best 2026 – Anant Anadi Vadnagar Archaeological Experiential Museum** (Vadnagar, **Mehsana district, Gujarat**): won in the **Exhibition Design** category of the **Red Dot Award: Brands & Communication Design 2026**, presented in **Berlin (Germany)**; designed by **Design Factory India (Noida)**; the **first Indian museum** to win the "Best of the Best" level; its galleries use **seven layers of rammed earth** for seven historical periods (about **2,500 years** of history); museum inaugurated **16 Jan 2025**. Earlier Gujarat Red Dot: **Smritivan Earthquake Museum, Bhuj (2023)**, Spatial Communication.
- **[Nov 2026] James Dyson Award 2026 – global winners:** **Sentinel** (Philippines) by structural engineer **Aldrei Ong** – a low-cost sensor that detects hidden **earthquake damage in concrete** buildings – **Global Sustainability Winner**; **Rumble Rims** (Harvard students) – an infrared eye-tracking headset for sideline **concussion** screening; each gets about **£30,000**; **2,294 entries**. India's Braille printer **RUDHRA** had reached the global Top 20.
- **[Nov 2026] Plant Genome Saviour Awards** at the **22nd Foundation Day of PPVFRA** (Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Authority), New Delhi – addressed by **Dr P.K. Mishra**, Principal Secretary to the PM; marks the **Silver Jubilee of the PPV&FR Act, 2001**; each year **5 Community Awards (₹10 lakh each)**, **10 Farmer Rewards (₹1.5 lakh)** and **20 Farmer Recognitions (₹1 lakh)**; PPVFRA set up **2005**, under the **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**.
- **[16 Nov 2026] 15th UNESCO–Madanjeet Singh Prize** (for the Promotion of Tolerance and Non-Violence) – **Samoa Victim Support Group**; given around the **International Day for Tolerance (16 Nov)**.
- **[Nov 2026] Kochon Prize 2026 (more facts):** winner **REACH** is based in **Chennai**; prize **US$65,000**; presented with the **Stop TB Partnership** at its **40th Board meeting (Indonesia)**; Kochon Foundation (South Korea) est. **1973**; earlier Indian winners – **Dr L.S. Chauhan (2006)**, **ICMR (2017)**, **Molbio Diagnostics (2024)**.
- **[Nov 2026] Kutch Copper Ltd** (Adani Enterprises subsidiary, smelter at **Mundra, Gujarat**) – **first Indian copper producer** to get the **Veramark Assurance** certification (formerly **Copper Mark**), aligned with **SDG 12**.
# Award Links of Persons in News
- **Pandit Manilal Nag** (died **9 Nov 2026**, Kolkata, 87) – sitar maestro of the **Bishnupur Gharana**; **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2001**, **Padma Shri 2020**.
- **Arpita Singh** (died **9 Nov 2026**, Delhi, 89) – modernist painter (figurative works on women); **Padma Bhushan 2011**, **Lalit Kala Akademi Fellowship 2014**.
- **Gurdial Singh Bhangu** (died Nov 2026, **Surrey, Canada**, 86) – coached the women's hockey team to **2002 Commonwealth Games gold (Manchester)** – the story behind ***Chak De! India***; **Dronacharya Award 2000** – the **first hockey coach** to get it.
- **William Nordhaus** (died **30 Oct 2026**, New Haven, 85) – **Nobel Economics 2018** (shared with **Paul Romer**) for integrating **climate change** into long-run macroeconomics (DICE model, **social cost of carbon**).
> ⚠ Trap: the Vadnagar museum won the **Red Dot "Best of the Best"** (Exhibition Design, Berlin) – not a UNESCO award; Bhuj's Smritivan had a Red Dot in 2023. **Sentinel** (Philippines) won the Dyson **Sustainability** prize; India's RUDHRA was only a Top-20 finalist.

# Cricket – U-19 Asia Cup and ICC Decisions
- **[14 Nov 2026] U-19 Asia Cup 2026** (Muscat, **Oman**, 5–14 Nov, 8 teams): **India beat Pakistan by one wicket** off the **last ball** at the **Al Amerat Cricket Ground**, chasing **338** (339/9); **record 9th title**, first since **2021**; captain **Lakshya Raichandani** (80); **Mohit Ulva** hit the winning runs; **Aaryavir Sehwag** – Player of the Tournament (**361 runs**); Pakistan were the defending champions (beat India by 191 runs in Dubai, 2025).
- **[16 Nov 2026] Jay Shah reappointed unopposed as ICC Chairman** for a **second two-year term** (ICC Board meetings, **Bali, Indonesia**); first took office **1 Dec 2024**, succeeding **Greg Barclay (New Zealand)**; at **35** he was the youngest ICC chair.
- **[15 Nov 2026] ICC calendar to 2035 (Bali):** **India – sole host of the 2029 Men's Champions Trophy (9–28 Oct 2029)**, its first Champions Trophy at home since **2006**; **India and Bangladesh** co-host the **2031 ODI World Cup (9 Oct – 23 Nov 2031)**; 2027 ODI WC – **South Africa, Zimbabwe, Namibia**; 2028 T20 WC – **Australia and New Zealand**; 2030 T20 WC – **England, Ireland, Scotland**; WTC finals 2029 and 2031 – **England**.
- **[23 Oct 2026] Sabbhineni Meghana** (AP; **Andhra Cricket Association**) retired from all formats at **30**: **3 ODIs, 17 T20Is** for India (debut 2022); WPL – **RCB** (title 2024) and Gujarat Giants.
# Football – SAFF Championship and Messi
- **[17 Nov 2026] SAFF Championship 2026 final** (**National Stadium, Dhaka**): **India 2–1 Pakistan** – Alamgir Ghazi (45+1') put Pakistan ahead; **Suhail Ahmad Bhat (60')** and **Sandip Mandi (88')** scored for India; Pakistan's **Junaid Shah** sent off (59', VAR); Pakistan's **first SAFF final**.
- India's **record-extending 10th SAFF title** and first **hat-trick of titles** (three successive editions); coach **Naushad Moosa**; captain **Chinglensana Singh Konsham**; **MVP and top scorer – Suhail Ahmad Bhat (4 goals)**; best goalkeeper **Arsh Anwer Shaikh**; India beat Bhutan 2–1 in the semi-final (14 Nov) and Pakistan 3–2 in the opener (5 Nov).
- **[Nov 2026] Lionel Messi** (Inter Miami) – **2026 MLS Golden Boot** with **26 goals** – the **first player to win it in consecutive seasons** (29 goals in 2025); sixth two-time winner.
# Badminton, Shooting and Multi-sport
- **[15 Nov 2026] Lakshya Sen – Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026** (BWF **Super 500**): beat **Koki Watanabe (Japan)** 13–21, 21–18, 21–14 – the **first Indian** to win it (held since **2023**); his **second straight Super 500 title** after the **Hylo Open**. BWF HQ – **Kuala Lumpur**.
- **[13 Nov 2026] Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games – India's final tally: 10 medals (2 G, 3 S, 5 B), 21st** – second-best after **13 medals at Buenos Aires 2018**; golds: **Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei** (Manipur, men's **50 kg boxing**, beat Ireland's Kristian Jubani) and **Gunjan** (women's **48 kg**) – India's **first YOG boxing golds**; top: **China 33 (18 G)**, Japan 28, Russia 14; first Olympic event on **African soil** (~2,650 athletes, 204 NOCs, 153 events in 25 sports).
- **[14 Nov 2026] ISSF World Championship 2026, Doha (1–14 Nov) – final:** **China** topped (27 medals: 13 G); **India 13 medals (2 G, 7 S, 4 B)** and **three LA28 quota places** – **Jaypal Malviya** (10 m air pistol, silver), **Niraj Kumar** (50 m rifle 3 positions, bronze), **Vivaan Kapoor** (trap, silver) – India's best opening quota haul.
- **[15 Nov 2026] Khelo India Youth Games 2026 (8th):** logo and mascot **"Neelamani"** (a bird-inspired character) unveiled by **Mansukh Mandaviya** and Telangana CM **A. Revanth Reddy**; Telangana, **11–22 Dec 2026**, six cities – **Hyderabad, Khammam, Karimnagar, Hanumakonda, Mahabubnagar, Nizamabad**; **softball** debuts; **sailing and Karra Samu** – demonstration sports; tagline "**Khel Ka Junoon, Telangana Ki Jaan Aur Pehchaan**".
- **[Nov 2026] IOA Athletes' Commission 2026–30:** **P.V. Sindhu – Chairperson**, **Harmanpreet Singh – Vice-Chairperson** (unopposed); members elected unopposed on 3 Nov incl. **Mirabai Chanu**; IOA elections on **5 Dec 2026**.
- **World Armwrestling Championships 2026, New Delhi (29 Oct – 6 Nov)** – India hosted for the **first time**, finished **5th** with **59 medals (9 G, 19 S, 31 B)**; Russia topped; 2027 edition in **Canada**.
- **[8 Nov 2026] F1 São Paulo Grand Prix (Interlagos):** **Lando Norris (McLaren)** won from pole ahead of **Max Verstappen** and Isack Hadjar; **Mercedes** clinched the **2026 Constructors' Championship** (its **9th**, first since 2021); Lewis Hamilton's **400th** Grand Prix.
- **Sunil Chhetri** – first male participant in the **FIFA Player Impact Programme 2026** (nine-month programme, 13-member cohort).
> ⚠ Trap: U-19 Asia Cup 2026 – India beat **Pakistan by 1 wicket** in **Muscat** (9th title); SAFF 2026 – India beat **Pakistan 2–1** in **Dhaka** (10th title). 2029 Champions Trophy – **India alone**; 2031 ODI World Cup – **India + Bangladesh**. YOG Dakar – Gunjan's final was won: India ended with **2 golds**.
~~ Sources: khaleejtimes.com, theweek.in, outlookindia.com (U-19 Asia Cup final, 14 Nov 2026); affairscloud 18 Nov 2026; outlookindia.com, timeslive.co.za (Jay Shah, 16 Nov 2026); gulfnews.com, theweek.in, newsonair.gov.in (ICC calendar); crictracker.com, freepressjournal.in (Meghana); the-aiff.com match reports (SAFF final, 17 Nov 2026); mlssoccer.com, intermiamicf.com (Messi Golden Boot); newsonair.gov.in, outlookindia.com (Lakshya Sen); newsonair.gov.in, openthemagazine.com, republicworld.com (YOG final); outlookindia.com and affairscloud 17 Nov 2026 (ISSF); newsonair.gov.in, gktoday.in (KIYG mascot); deccanchronicle.com, outlookindia.com (IOA AC); affairscloud 11-12 Nov 2026 (armwrestling, Brazil GP, Chhetri); planetf1.com, latintimes.com (Brazil GP)

title: Latest: 5-18 Nov 2026
md:
# Space
- **[13–14 Nov 2026] SpaceX Starship Flight 15:** **Ship 42** was caught in mid-air by the launch tower's "**chopsticks**" (Mechazilla) at **Starbase, Texas** – the **first catch of a Starship upper stage** (earlier only Super Heavy boosters were caught); about **22.5 hours** and **14 orbits** in space; the **Super Heavy booster** aborted its catch and was lost over the **Gulf of Mexico**.
- **[Nov 2026] ISRO – upgraded PSLV third stage (PS3):** ground **static test** of the solid motor at **SDSC SHAR, Sriharikota (AP)**, after the anomalies in **PSLV-C61/EOS-09** and **PSLV-C62/EOS-N1**; changes – nozzle improvements, stronger interfaces, **redundant sealing**, extra **non-destructive testing**.
- **[5 Nov 2026] GSLV-F19 cryogenic engine** – **flight acceptance test** (about **200 s**) at the **ISRO Propulsion Complex, Mahendragiri (Tamil Nadu)**; the engine will power the third stage of **GSLV-F19** carrying **NVS-04** (NavIC) in **2027**.
# Telecom, AI and Technology Alliances
- **[16 Nov 2026] India re-elected to the ITU Council for 2027–30** at the **ITU Plenipotentiary Conference PP-26, Doha (9–27 Nov)** – one of **13 Region E (Asia & Australasia)** seats on the **48-member** Council; **Doreen Bogdan-Martin** re-elected Secretary-General; ITU HQ **Geneva**, est. **1865**.
- **[15 Nov 2026] San Francisco Declaration** – signed at the **Pax Silica Founders Retreat (San Francisco)** by **10 countries** (USA, India, Australia, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, UAE, UK) to secure **critical technologies and AI supply chains**; convened by US Under Secretary **Jacob Helberg**; India's delegation led by **S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY**.
- **[12 Nov 2026] IAF UDAAN AI applications** – unveiled by **Rajnath Singh** at the **Air Force Commanders' Conference 2026** (theme "**The Year of Empowerment: Maximising Efficiency Through Decentralisation**"); UDAAN's **AI Centre of Excellence** opened **10 July 2022**.
- **[Nov 2026] 'Sanskriti' AI search platform** (Ministry of Culture, on **culture.gov.in**): one search across about **65 portals** (Gyan Bharatam, Abhilekh Patal, Indian Culture, Mera Gaon Meri Dharohar); **22 Indian languages** via **BHASHINI**; uses NLP, knowledge graphs and **RAG** to give cited answers from official sources only.
- **[11–15 Nov 2026] 2nd India–Italy Science and Innovation Dialogue (Rome):** led by **Dr Jitendra Singh**; Letter of Intent between **DST and ICTP** (Trieste) for an **India–ICTP Co-operation Fund**; India commits **over €7 million (5 years)** to redevelop beamlines at **Elettra Sincrotrone Trieste**.
- **[Nov 2026] IL-76MD 'Gajraj'** of the IAF landed at **Mudh-Nyoma Airbase (Ladakh)** at **13,629 ft (~4,154 m)** – a world record for the **highest landing** by this aircraft type.
# Health and Agri-biotech
- **[15 Nov 2026] National Health Accounts (NHA) Estimates 2023-24 (MoHFW):** **Government Health Expenditure ₹4.14 lakh crore** (₹1.30 lakh crore in 2013-14) = **1.43% of GDP** (States ~68%, Union ~32%); **out-of-pocket expenditure fell from 64.2% to 42.7%** of Total Health Expenditure; THE **₹9,52,122 crore (3.29% of GDP)**, **₹6,801 per capita**.
- **WHO Global TB Report 2026 (more facts):** data from **187 countries/areas**; **10.6 million** fell ill and **1.13 million** died of TB in 2025; **eight countries ≈ 67%** of cases – **India 25%**, Indonesia 10%, Philippines 6.8%, China 6.5%, Pakistan 6.4%, Nigeria 4.9%, DR Congo 3.9%, Bangladesh 3.7%.
- **[15 Nov 2026] Centre of Excellence for Genome Editing in Horticultural Crops** – opened by **Dr M.L. Jat** (DG, ICAR) at **ICAR-IIHR, Bengaluru**, with a **BSL-II lab**; target crops **tomato, chilli, papaya, grapes, pomegranate**; a Farmers' Advanced Training Centre also opened.
> ⚠ Trap: Starship Flight 15 caught the **ship (upper stage)** – the booster was lost. The PS3 test was at **Sriharikota**, the cryogenic engine test at **Mahendragiri**. India is on the ITU **Council** (48 members), not the Radio Regulations Board. NHA 2023-24: OOPE **42.7%**, GHE **1.43% of GDP**.

title: Latest: 5-18 Nov 2026
md:
# Cyclone Akvan (AP angle)
- **[16 Nov 2026] Cyclonic Storm Akvan** formed from a deep depression over the **south Bay of Bengal** (17:30 IST); name from **Iran** – after **Akvan-e-Div**, a demon in Ferdowsi's ***Shahnameh***; named by **RSMC New Delhi** from the **WMO/ESCAP Panel** list.
- **IMD forecast (17 Nov):** a severe cyclonic storm by 17 Nov night and a **very severe cyclonic storm** by **19 Nov**; landfall on the **Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast between Nellore and Tuni** around **noon, 20 Nov 2026**, winds **120–130 km/h gusting to 145 km/h**; heavy rain alerts for **coastal AP, Yanam, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry**, and south **Odisha**.
- Akvan is the **third cyclone in about a month** to hit AP, after **Arnab** (Bangladesh-named, crossed near Narsapur, 28 Oct) and **Murasu** (India-named, 1–3 Nov).
# COP31 – Second Week (Antalya, 9–20 Nov 2026)
- **[16 Nov 2026] Bhupender Yadav** (arrived **15 Nov**) met **Simon Stiell** (UNFCCC Executive Secretary) and **Chris Bowen** (COP31 President of Negotiations); India seeks a **COP31 decision to launch a Climate Finance Work Programme** – finance as a developed-country obligation under **Article 9.1** of the Paris Agreement, predictable, mostly **public and concessional**.
- India's other asks: **Global Goal on Adaptation** indicators to stay **voluntary** (not a condition for finance); a Party-driven **Just Transition Work Programme**; non-punitive **Global Stocktake**; Yadav co-facilitates the **ministerial consultations on mitigation** with **Carsten Schneider (Germany)**; side events on **LeadIT 3.0 (with Sweden)** and the **International Big Cat Alliance**.

# New Species
- **[Nov 2026] *Echinorhinus roinee* (Indian Bramble Shark)** – a **new deep-sea shark** described by **ZSI and ICAR-CMFRI** (supported by MoES's **Deep Ocean Mission**); long mistaken for the Atlantic bramble shark ***E. brucus***; type specimens from **Sakthikulangara Fishing Harbour, Kollam (Kerala)**; up to **3 m**, lives at **350–450 m** on continental slopes; named after **Roinee**, daughter of ZSI Director **Dhriti Banerjee**; published in ***Records of the Zoological Survey of India*, Vol. 126**.
- **[11 Nov 2026] Five new horned frogs (genus *Jingophrys*) in Arunachal Pradesh** – by the **University of Delhi and Harvard University**, in ***Royal Society Open Science***: ***J. tanogogo*** – **India's first documented snail-eating frog** (first in family **Megophryidae**), ***J. taniitatii*** (honours the **Tanii/Apatani** people of **Ziro Valley**), ***J. siangensis*** (Siang), ***J. hrdy***, ***J. wularsoni***.
- **[Nov 2026] *Liocheles similipalensis*** – a new **scorpion** from **Similipal Tiger Reserve (Mayurbhanj, Odisha)**, in the journal ***Euscorpius***; the **first record of genus *Liocheles* in Odisha**; black body with a bluish sheen (44–53 mm).
